They favor the windcleaver blade and are extremely agile despite their bulky build. At this Yiga Clan rank, they have mastered a technique that allows them to manipulate the very earth. By striking the ground, they can create stone pillars and blasts of air.|Hyrule Compendium|BotW}} They can be found patrolling the [[Yiga Clan Hideout]], and if they spot [[Link]] in the hideout, they will close all doors and exits while calling in back up. After [[Master Kohga]] is defeated, they will also start appearing randomly to attack Link. Yiga Blademasters attack with [[Windcleaver]]s that send blasts of air at long distances. They can also use the [[Earthwake Technique]] to create fissures in the ground, which produce [[Updraft]]s that Link can use to [[Gliding|Glide]] before a stone pillar emerges from them. A shot to the head with the [[Bow]] can stun Yiga Blademasters, opening them for attacks. When defeated, they flee, leaving behind their Windcleaver and [[Mighty Bananas]]. During the [[Side Quest]] "[[The Stolen Heirloom]]", Link must defeat a Yiga Blademaster in order to retrieve the [[Sheikah Heirloom]] that grants access to the [[Lakna Rokee Shrine]].{{Cite|It turned out that the heirloom thieves who struck Impa's manor belonged to the Yiga Clan. The incident was revenge for Dorian attempting to leave the guild of assassins. After you solved the problem, you returned the heirloom and discovered a new ancient shrine.|Adventure Log|BotW}} ====Drops==== {{Collapsible |header= Drops of Yiga Blademaster |collapse= true |content= {{Tabs |- | Normal | {{Drop Table |game= BotW |- | Mighty Bananas | 1-2
| 100 % |- | Amber | 1-2 | 10 % |- | Opal | 1-2 | 1 % |- | Topaz | 1-2 | 1 % |- | Ruby | 1-2 | 1 % |- | Sapphire | 1-2 | 1 % }} }} }} ==={{TotK|-}}=== {{Compendium/Extract/TotK|Yiga Blademaster}} Yiga Blademasters reappear in {{TotK}}, acting similarly to how they did in {{BotW}}. They now wield [[Eightfold Longblade]]s with visible [[Gloom]] markings rather than [[Windcleaver]]s. They can disguise themselves as [[Tree]]s. If [[Link]] is wearing the [[Yiga Clan Attire]], he is able to speak to Yiga Blademasters without being attacked. In addition, they are mentioned to be the overseers of the [[Yiga|Yiga Clan]]'s [[Depths]] operations.{{Fact}} ==Other Appearances== ==={{AoC|-}}=== {{Noncanon|Start}} Yiga Blademasters appear in {{AoC}} as [[Powerful Foe]]s. They fight the same way as in {{BotW}}, though their [[Weak-Point Gauge]]s can be exploited with [[Rune|Sheikah Runes]]. They also speak, similar to the Yiga Footsoldiers, in instances such as when they are defeated in battle.{{Cite|Master Kohga...I failed.|Yiga Blademaster|AoC}} After [[Astor]] uses the souls of some Yiga Footsoldiers to revive the four blights, [[Master Kohga]] and [[Sooga]] turn against him. The rest of the Yiga Clan then follow suit, using the [[Forces|Hyrulean Army]] to exact vengeance on Astor. {{Noncanon|End}} ==Nomenclature== {{Nomenclature}} ==Gallery== File:BotW Yiga Blademaster.png|{{Game Label|{{BotW|-}}}}Link battling a Yiga Blademaster File:BotW Yiga Blademaster Concept Artwork.png|{{Game Label|{{BotW|-}}}}Concept artwork of Yiga Blademaster from {{CaC|-}} File:TotK Yiga Blademaster Eightfold Longblade Model.png|{{Game Label|{{TotK|-}}}}Model of a Yiga Blademaster wielding an Eightfold Longblade ==See Also== {{See Also| * Yiga Clan * Yiga Footsoldier }} {{Ref| {{Cite|Betrayed by the seer and with the Yiga Clan on the brink of annihilation, Master Kohga and Blademaster Sooga narrowly escaped death.|Narration|AoC}} }} {{Categories |Powerful Enemies, Sheikah, Yiga |bosses= AoC |enemies= BotW, TotK }}
